newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, potential for mild growth.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, potential for mild growth.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in moderate trade on Wednesday and analysts foresaw mild growth at a slower pace for most issues in the near future.
"It seems that the situation is generally improving," said one trader.
Lower prices and slower trade dominated much of the last week as large investors stayed away from the market -- a trend analysts blamed largely on recent unrest in neighbouring Bosnia.
Four of 14 active issues rose on Wednesday, six fell and four were flat. Volume dipped to 6,962 from 10,016 shares, turnover was slightly higher at 4.9 million kuna.
Varazdinska Banka topped the list of gainers, jumping 7,000 kuna to 35,000 with only three shares sold.
Dalmatinska Banka stayed flat at 485 kuna on volume of 100 units and Trgovacka Banka added 20 kuna to 1,620, trading 50 shares in a first deal since last November.
Traders predicted the three bank stocks could soon forge ahead.
"Their shares are much on offer, but everybody is waiting to see if they are to be fully-listed (on the Zagreb Stock Exchange)," the trader said.
Zagreb's Hotel Intercontinental rebounded 50 kuna to its October price of 170 kuna, selling 49 shares.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka was also among gainers, rising 21 kuna to 1,735 on volume of 1,709 shares. Drugs firm Pliva inched down three kuna to 457, with 280 shares sold.

Global depositary receipts (GDRs) of both firms fell in London due to a stronger dollar, dealers said. Pliva's GDRs traded in a $15/15.25 range and Zagrebacka's traded lower at $29.515 on Seaq International.
Zagrebacka's preference E-series stock dipped 17 kuna to 1,033 with 90 shares changing hands.
Biggest decliner brewery Karlovacka Pivovara lost 10 kuna to 225, trading eight shares.
Most active food processor Podravka remained flat at 305 kuna on volume of 3,098 shares. Confectioner Kras fell 15 kuna to 500.
Hoteliers Laguna and Riviera were flat at 1,400 and 180 kuna respectively.
